You've hit **both** of Marketo's most common Velocity fallback traps:

## The problems

1. **`:default=` does not work on Email Script tokens at all** — that syntax only works on simple tokens like `{{lead.First Name:default=there}}`. Adobe is explicit that Email Script tokens don't support it.

2. **`$display.alt()` does not work on lead fields** — Marketo ensures lead fields are always empty strings (`""`), never `null`. Since `$display.alt` only substitutes when the value is `null`, the fallback never fires.

## The fix

Handle the fallback **inside the Velocity** using `.isEmpty()`:

```velocity
#if( $lead.AccountManagerName.isEmpty() )
our team##
#else
$!{lead.AccountManagerName}##
#end
```

Reference it in the email as just `{{my.accountManagerScript}}` — no `:default=`.

The `##` at the end of each line suppresses trailing newlines, which matters when this appears mid-sentence.

If you're building a reusable pattern, here's a macro version:

```velocity
#macro( displayIfFilled $checkValue $fallbackValue )
#if( !($checkValue.isEmpty()) )
$!checkValue##
#else
$!fallbackValue##
#end
#end

#displayIfFilled($lead.AccountManagerName, "our team")
```

Both approaches work — the first is simpler for a single field, the second is cleaner if you're applying the pattern to multiple fields in one script.

This is a well-known Marketo quirk: **script tokens completely ignore the `:default=` parameter**. Unlike regular tokens, when a script returns null or empty, Marketo just renders nothing—it won't fall back to your default value.

The issue with your `$display.alt()` attempt is likely that it only handles null values, not empty strings. If `AccountManagerName` is an empty string rather than truly null, `alt()` won't catch it.

Here's the fix—handle the default inside your Velocity script:

```velocity
#if( $lead.AccountManagerName && !$lead.AccountManagerName.isEmpty() )
${lead.AccountManagerName}
#else
our team
#end
```

Or more concisely:

```velocity
#set( $manager = $lead.AccountManagerName )
#if( !$manager || $manager.isEmpty() )our team#{else}${manager}#end
```

This checks for both null and empty string, which covers the common cases where the field exists but has no value.

The key principle: **any default/fallback logic for script tokens must live inside the script itself**—you can't rely on Marketo's token-level defaults.

That's the **reserved word trap** — one of Marketo's most confusing gotchas.

Every Marketo email is assembled using Velocity under the hood, so these 13 strings are **reserved anywhere in an email**, even when there's no scripting at all:

```
#if  #else  #elseif  #foreach  #end  #set  #define
#macro  #include  #parse  #break  #stop  #evaluate
```

You have `#end` in **two places**, and both are breaking validation:

1. The URL fragment: `#end-user-agreement`
2. The body copy: "to the #end"

## Fixes

**In the URL**, percent-encode the first character after the `#`:
```
https://example.com/legal/#%65nd-user-agreement
```
(The `%65` is the hex code for `e` — this renders as `#end-user-agreement` in the browser but won't trigger Velocity's parser.)

**In the visible text**, insert a word joiner HTML entity after the `#`:
```html
from the beginning right through to the #⁠end
```
(Renders as "to the #end" but breaks the reserved word pattern.)

Make both changes and the email should validate. This is documented Marketo behavior — your exact examples (`#end-user-privacy-policy` in a URL and "to the #end" in copy) appear in Adobe's own troubleshooting docs as real-world breakage cases.
